annotations.keyFindings: At 2 mmol/L, pooled sensitivity 0.65 and specificity 0.72 for sepsis with organ dysfunction across 14 studies; at 4 mmol/L, 0.31 and 0.94.
annotations.limitations: Substantial heterogeneity; unblinded reference diagnoses; spectrum bias where only unwell-looking patients were tested.
annotations.notes: The review closest to the triage question.

annotations.keyFindings: Lactate of 4 mmol/L or more associated with higher in-hospital mortality (unadjusted odds ratios 2.1 to 6.8 across 22 studies).
annotations.limitations: Mixed sample types; few triage measurements; unadjusted estimates.

annotations.keyFindings: Capillary values about 0.3 mmol/L higher than venous, with wider limits at high values and poor perfusion.
annotations.notes: Relevant to whether capillary triage values can be read against thresholds from venous studies.

annotations.keyFindings: Pathways with triage lactate reduced median time to antibiotics by 38 minutes, with no clear effect on mortality; more patients moved to resuscitation.
annotations.limitations: Before-after studies with multiple simultaneous changes.

annotations.keyFindings: Among patients with lactate below 2 mmol/L, 9 percent had sepsis with organ dysfunction and 3 percent died; false reassurance more common in older patients and those on beta blockers.
annotations.limitations: Negative predictive value depends on prevalence in each study.
annotations.notes: Directly addresses the investigator's main worry.

annotations.keyFindings: Corrected covered area 18 percent across 19 reviews; five primary studies appeared in more than ten reviews; opposite conclusions often shared primary studies.
annotations.limitations: Citation matrix built from reported reference lists.

annotations.keyFindings: Most of 34 biomarker reviews were rated at critically low confidence; only three at high confidence.
annotations.limitations: Predates recent reviews; single appraiser with sample checking.

annotations.keyFindings: Recommends lactate for adults with suspected infection meeting a physiological criterion, treats 4 mmol/L or more as a senior-review trigger, and advises against lowering priority on a normal value.
annotations.limitations: Partly consensus-based on reviews of low confidence.

synthesis: Eight retrieved records, appraised at abstract level. The syntheses agree that a raised lactate marks higher risk, but a pooled accuracy review shows that a threshold of 2 mmol/L misses about a third of patients with sepsis with organ dysfunction, and a pooled analysis finds that about one in eleven patients with a normal lactate has such sepsis. Reviews overlap heavily in their primary studies and are mostly of critically low confidence, which explains much of their disagreement. Pathway studies show faster antibiotics but no clear mortality benefit and hint at crowding costs. The evidence supports an umbrella review that corrects for overlap, rates confidence and reports false reassurance and false alarms as the outcomes that matter for a triage rule.
gradeRationale: Reviews of mostly unblinded, heterogeneous accuracy studies with heavy overlap and low confidence; consistent direction on risk, serious inconsistency on thresholds.
summary: Eight records appraised; five claims; certainty low.
